content.title: About
content.content: Sorghum is a warm‑climate cereal grain cultivated worldwide. Organic puffed sorghum is made by thermally expanding whole grains, resulting in light, crunchy, and nutritious flakes. The product is gluten‑free and suitable for vegans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sorghum is one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 5,000 years.
Organic sorghum is produced without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers.
Puffed sorghum is commonly used in gluten‑free breakfast cereals and snacks.
Sorghum has higher iron and magnesium levels than many other grains.
In some countries sorghum is also used for bio‑ethanol production.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Sorghum provides a notable amount of iron, supporting normal blood formation.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium from sorghum helps maintain normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Puffed sorghum raises blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: The product is safe for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some people may experience an allergic reaction to sorghum.

items.title: Calorie density in large portions
items.content: While the flakes are light, overeating can lead to excess calorie intake.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; a varied diet is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Puffed sorghum can be enjoyed as a snack, mixed into granola, yogurt, smoothies, baked into bars, or used as a crunchy topping for salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flakes in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For long‑term storage, keep them refrigerated.
